RSI is a dynamic group of companies that has provided services to major federal clients and Fortune 500 engineering and construction companies since 1996. RSI is headquartered in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and is a wholly owned operating company of ASRC Industrial (AIS). AIS is a wholly owned operating company of Arctic Slope Regional Corporation (ASRC), an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC). Through ASRC, we are a certified Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) and Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), and we also offer 8(a) options.

Position Summary

RSI is recruiting for a Field Technician who will work as part of a team that operates and maintains a network of remote instrumentation, often referred to as Operational Technology (OT), and interacts with personnel assigned to provide site operations support for system operations typically located at remote sites. This instrumentation primarily collects environmental data but is also used to administer remote control and monitor treatment processes at remote sites. The remote telemetry network is composed of data loggers, meteorological sensors, water level transducers, flow meters, and various other sensors and equipment. This instrumentation includes the site-based SOARS (System Operations and Analysis at Remote Sites) units as a critical piece of the infrastructure. This position supports infrastructure that controls and maintains environmental monitoring and remediation systems for DOE Office of Legacy Management. This position is responsible for ensuring safe execution of work conducted by the project team.

Job Title:
Field Technician

Location(s):
Grand Junction, CO

Status:
Full-Time

FLSA:
Exempt

Hiring Range:
$ 60,000.00 - $70,000.00 per year. (The anticipated starting salary is based on the posted minimum requirements for this position. The offered salary will be based upon the selected applicant’s education, training, and experience.)

This position is required to travel 25-50% of the time.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Assist in collection and maintenance of an asset inventory for all OT related systems spanning the full lifecycle.
Troubleshoot and diagnose errors and inconsistencies with endpoint devices and integration into SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) and telemetry environments.
Coordinate with the SOARS and OT teams to ensure that equipment is patched according to cyber security directives. Diligently plan and track software patching.
Coordinate with OT and SOARS teams to track, apply, and document password updates for applicable OT devices.
Coordinate closely with site operations and other relevant teams to communicate any potential disruptions to normal operations. Communicate with subject matter experts and site leads to describe how collected data relates to in-the-field variables.
Respond to unplanned disruptions in a timely manner to help resolve issues relating to OT telemetry. Some OT telemetry administration may be done remotely while some may require travel to various LM sites across the US.
Provide guidance and support in the ongoing upkeep of the SCADA/EMCS/telemetry systems. This system upkeep may include EMCS (Energy Management and Control Systems).
Verify accuracy of data and equipment, metering values, alarm points, etc. often working with other SMEs (subject matter experts) to identify and establish standards for specific systems.
Coordinate with SOARS and OT teams to perform scheduled preventive maintenance tasks, such as checking, cleaning, calibrating, or repairing equipment, to detect and prevent problems.
Participate in training or continuing education activities to stay abreast of industry advances.
Monitor and respond to system generated alerts.
Travel to assigned DOE LM sites to install, maintain, and replace equipment (26-49 % travel).
Participate in the creation and review of operation and maintenance documentation and any other applicable documentation.
Complete work-specific safety and health documents, including job safety analysis, pre-job safety briefs, and work authorization forms (e.g., confined space entry, penetration permit, ladder inspection, heat stress). Ensure these forms are properly stored, according to record management requirements.
Identify, troubleshoot, and resolve equipment malfunctions; replace defective components or parts using hand tools or power tools; and work with manufacturers or field representatives to fix equipment or to procure replacement parts.
Maintain working knowledge of various low voltage instruments, including but not limited to weighing rain gauges, tipping bucket rain gauges, sonic anemometers, solar irradiance sensors, flow meters, automatic valves, pressure sensors, temperature sensors, relative humidity sensors, temperature sensors, barometric pressure sensors, water level sensors, and soil moisture sensors.

Integrate software or hardware components, using computers, microprocessors, or control architecture.
Clearly communicate site configuration changes to all applicable stakeholders.
Participate in training or continuing education activities to stay abreast of industry advances.
Install and maintain low voltage electrical control systems, sensors, or electrical equipment, including data loggers, meteorologic stations, transducers, flow meters, and programmable logic controllers.
Maintain equipment logs that record performance problems, repairs, calibrations, or tests.
Inspect components of equipment for accurate assembly and installation or for defects, such as loose connections or frayed wires.
Calibrate testing instruments and perform calibration verification checks on installed or repaired equipment to meet prescribed data quality objectives.
Consult with stakeholders to plan and design the installation and layout of equipment or to resolve problems related to system operation or maintenance. Participate in project planning and design drawing reviews for various types of projects.
Study blueprints, schematics, manuals, or other specifications to determine installation procedures and to troubleshoot systems.
Receive and maintain specialized training, including but not limited to Confined Space Entry, Radiological Worker II, CPR/First Aid, Lock Out/Tag Out, and UTV Operation.

At IBM, the work is about building things that matter. You will be working on real problems in a mission environment where the output of your work is used, not just presented.

We are looking for a hands-on data and engineering professional who can take messy, incomplete information and turn it into something useful and clear. This role is about going from raw data to real understanding and doing it in a way that people can act on immediately, with confidence.

You will work across the full lifecycle of work. That includes getting data, shaping it, building models where needed, and delivering outputs that help people make decisions. This is not a role where someone hands you a clean dataset or defined problem.

*** Candidate is required to have US Citizenship for this role without exception. Candidates must also have an approved, active US Government Top Secret/SCI security clearance with Full Scope Polygraph

who works across data, systems, and analysis to deliver outcomes that are usable in real mission conditions.

The focus is on building work that holds up in operational use, not just in controlled environments.

You will contribute across the workflow, from how data is handled through how it is used, making practical decisions that balance technical quality with mission needs.

Work directly with raw and incomplete data, determining how to structure, process, and use it effectively.
Develop and apply models and analytical methods to identify meaningful patterns, behaviors, and signals.
Build and support data pipelines that enable consistent, repeatable processing across datasets.
Integrate internal and external models into working systems and adjust them as conditions or data changes.
Operate effectively in secure and constrained environments where tradeoffs are required.

About IronHorn Enterprises

IronHorn Enterprises is a growing real estate investment and development firm specializing in industrial and commercial properties across key markets. We are committed to excellence, innovation, and the continued growth of both our portfolio and our team.

Position Overview

IronHorn Enterprises is seeking an organized, motivated, and detail-oriented Project Coordinator to support our Construction Management team. This position will work closely with the Senior Commercial Construction Project Manager, Commercial Construction Project Manager, and Preconstruction Manager to coordinate projects from initial site evaluation and preconstruction through active construction and closeout.
This position has a significant administrative component. The Project Coordinator will be responsible for maintaining project documentation, coordinating schedules and meetings, tracking action items, preparing reports, organizing electronic files, and following up with internal and external stakeholders. Candidates should be comfortable spending a substantial portion of their time performing detailed administrative and document-control work.
The ideal candidate is proactive, dependable, highly organized, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone interested in building a career in commercial construction and real estate development while gaining exposure to preconstruction, project management, and field operations.

Key Responsibilities

Administrative and Team Support

Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Construction Management team.
Coordinate calendars, meetings, site visits, property tours, inspections, and contractor walkthroughs.
Prepare and distribute meeting agendas, minutes, action-item lists, and follow-up communications.
Track open items, deadlines, approvals, and team deliverables to ensure timely completion.
Maintain project contact lists, calendars, departmental resources, and standardized templates.
Prepare correspondence, reports, presentations, spreadsheets, and executive-level project updates.
Assist with invoice routing, purchase orders, contract documentation, and internal approval processes.
Organize and maintain accurate electronic project files using established naming and filing procedures.
Support communication and coordination among Construction, Preconstruction, Facilities Management, Leasing, Finance, Legal, and Real Estate teams.
Perform general administrative and project-related duties as assigned.

Project Coordination

Support the planning and execution of multiple commercial construction projects.
Assist with project schedules, milestone tracking, action items, and deadline management.
Communicate with contractors, vendors, consultants, tenants, and internal stakeholders to keep projects moving forward.
Follow up on outstanding project items and escalate potential delays or concerns to the appropriate Project Manager.
Assist with project kickoff, progress, and closeout activities.
Help coordinate access to properties and active construction areas.

Preconstruction and Bidding Support

Assist with preparing requests for proposals, bid invitations, scopes of work, and bid packages.
Coordinate pre-bid walkthroughs and distribute relevant plans, specifications, and project information.
Track contractor and vendor questions, proposals, clarifications, and required follow-up.
Organize subcontractor and vendor bids and assist with bid comparisons.
Support material takeoffs, quantity reviews, and preliminary cost-estimating activities.
Maintain contractor, vendor, and historical project cost information.

Collaborate with the Preconstruction and Project Management teams to support the procurement of project materials and equipment

Assist with obtaining vendor quotes, comparing pricing, preparing purchase orders, and coordinating required approvals.
Track material and equipment selections, submittals, lead times, fabrication schedules, and delivery dates.
Maintain procurement logs and follow up with vendors and contractors regarding order status, availability, and outstanding information.
Identify long-lead items and potential procurement delays and promptly communicate concerns to the appropriate Project Manager.
Coordinate material and equipment deliveries with vendors, contractors, project schedules, and site-access requirements.
Maintain organized records of quotes, purchase orders, approvals, warranties, and other procurement-related documentation.

Project Documentation and Document Control

Maintain complete, organized, and accurate project records throughout the project lifecycle.
Track RFIs, submittals, change orders, proposals, contracts, permits, meeting minutes, and closeout documents.
Maintain current drawings, specifications, schedules, photographs, and project correspondence.
Manage document versions and distribution to ensure team members are working from current information.
Monitor required documentation and follow up with contractors, vendors, and consultants regarding missing or incomplete items.
Assist with assembling warranties, operations manuals, as-built drawings, lien releases, and other closeout documentation.

Budget and Contract Administration

Assist with tracking project budgets, commitments, invoices, purchase orders, and change orders.
Review invoices and supporting documentation for completeness before routing them for approval.
Maintain cost logs and help identify discrepancies between approved budgets, contracts, and actual expenses.
Support the preparation of project financial reports and budget updates.
Coordinate with Finance and other internal departments regarding project documentation and payments.

Field and Quality Support

Attend project sites and document construction progress through notes and photographs.
Help monitor project activities for alignment with approved plans, schedules, scopes, and quality expectations.
Assist with tracking punch-list items, corrective work, inspections, and closeout requirements.
Communicate field observations and potential issues to the appropriate Project Manager.
Help maintain professional and productive relationships with contractors, tenants, and project partners.

Qualifications

Associate or bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Business, Project Management, or a related field preferred.
One to three years of experience in construction, project coordination, administrative support, property management, facilities, real estate, or a related field preferred; relevant internships will be considered.
Strong administrative, organizational, and time-management skills.
Ability to manage detailed records, multiple calendars, competing deadlines, and frequent follow-up.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining complete and accurate documentation.
Ability to take initiative, follow through on assignments, and work effectively in a collaborative environment.
Working knowledge of commercial construction processes and terminology is preferred.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings is preferred.
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
Experience with project management, estimating, or document-management platforms such as Procore, Bluebeam, PlanSwift, or Microsoft Project is a plus.
Familiarity with AutoCAD, Revit, SketchUp, or similar design software is a plus but not required.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel locally to project sites as needed.

Working Conditions

This position is primarily office-based and includes a substantial amount of administrative, computer, scheduling, reporting, and document-management work.
Regular visits to active construction sites and company properties will also be required.
Occasional travel to project sites, contractor meetings, or other company locations may be necessary.
Site visits may involve walking on uneven surfaces, climbing stairs, and wearing required personal protective equipment.
The role requires the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing project priorities.

What We Offer

Hands-on experience across preconstruction, project management, and commercial real estate development.
Exposure to projects through every stage, from initial evaluation and estimating through construction and closeout.
A collaborative environment with direct mentorship from experienced construction professionals.
Opportunities for professional development and advancement within a growing organization.

Conduct timely follow-up on new and existing customer opportunities, including proactive outreach when appropriate. Recognize non-standard or complex situations and escalate them to the appropriate team member for resolution.

Communicate clearly and professionally with customers and internal teams across multiple channels, building trust and delivering exceptional service.

Maintain proactive communication with customers throughout the project lifecycle, clarify next steps, and solicit feedback.

Monitor project progress, support smooth handoffs between teams, and help resolve issues that may affect the customer experience or project timelines.

Support effective use of CRM, program-tracking, and customer information systems through accurate data entry, process documentation, user support, and coordination with IT.

Coordinate with utilities, lenders, contractors, and other program partners to support accurate and timely project, incentive, and financing processing and to troubleshoot issues as needed.

Contribute to continuous improvement efforts by supporting documentation, training, and process refinement in collaboration with internal teams and system partners.

Customer focused and relationship oriented, with demonstrated active listening, empathy, and the ability to guide customers toward appropriate solutions.

Reliable and professional, with the ability to meet established deadlines and service expectations. 

Proficiency with CRM platforms, Microsoft Office, workflow tools, and other business systems, with a strong commitment to data accuracy.
